# Subo

Subo is a survey and poll app trusted by 15,000+ Discord communities. It lets community managers, developers, and AI agents create conversational surveys and polls, collect responses, and analyze results — all inside Discord or on the web.

## Subo API

The Subo Public REST API (v1) gives developers and AI agents programmatic access to create, manage, and analyze conversational surveys and polls inside Discord communities and on the web.

AI agents can use this API to:
- Automatically generate full survey scripts from natural language intents or specific scripts
- Create, open, and manage survey projects
- Retrieve responses and trigger AI analysis
- React to real-time events via webhooks (project opened/closed, response submitted, analysis completed)

## Use Subo from an agent (MCP)

Subo runs an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over the same API, so an AI app can act on a community directly instead of calling REST endpoints.

- Endpoint: `https://api.subo.ai/mcp` (streamable HTTP)
- Auth, two ways:
  - **OAuth 2.1 (recommended; no key to handle).** Clients that support MCP authorization discover it from the 401: protected-resource metadata at `https://api.subo.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`, authorization server `https://app.subo.gg` (PKCE S256, client ID metadata documents or dynamic client registration, scope `mcp`, rotating refresh tokens). The person signs in with Discord, picks one community where they are an Admin and an access level (admin or creator), and approves. Works in claude.ai and Claude Desktop (Settings > Connectors > Add custom connector, URL `https://api.subo.ai/mcp`) and in Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http --scope user subo https://api.subo.ai/mcp`, restart, then `/mcp` to authenticate). The connection appears on the Account page as "Connected through OAuth" and can be revoked there; unused for 90 days, it asks to sign in again.
  - **API key header**, for clients that cannot sign in: `Authorization: Bearer sbo_live_…`, using an API key of type "Bot or agent" created by a community Admin on the Account page under API Access (https://app.subo.gg/app/account). The confirmation panel shows a ready-to-paste config. Claude Code: `claude mcp add --transport http --scope user subo https://api.subo.ai/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer sbo_live_…"` (run in a terminal, then restart Claude Code).
  - Either way, the access level (admin or creator) caps what the agent can do. Only community Admins can connect an app.
- One connection = one community. No operation takes a community id; the key's community is implied. The key acts with its owner's current access and loses it within about ten minutes of the owner losing it.
- 44 operations, each labeled with one of four tiers. Read-only and normal changes need no special care. **Outward** operations reach real people (opening or closing a project, granting XP or accomplishments, firing a test webhook); **Destructive** operations delete data or invalidate a secret. Confirm both with the human before calling them.
- Prompts (workflows the server ships, shown as slash commands in Claude Code, e.g. `/subo:weekly_review`): `weekly_review` (optional `days`, default 14) reviews recent projects, responses and analysis and proposes the next project, read-only until approved; `build_from_goal` (`goal`) clones or drafts a script, validates it, and stops before `open_project`. Claude Code passes only the first whitespace-separated word as a prompt argument, so a multi-word `goal` arrives truncated there.
- Resources: `subo://guide/authoring` (read before writing a script: block types, scales, piping, scoring), `subo://recipes` and `subo://recipes/{slug}`, `subo://openapi`, `subo://community`.
- Deliberately not available through MCP: creating, rotating or deleting API keys; changing a member's access level; connecting a new verified-audience source (it requires a human browser sign-in).
- Setup guide: https://subo.gg/blog/connect-discord-community-to-ai-agent/

## Docs

- [API Quickstart & Recipes](https://subo.gg/api): Static, crawlable quickstart plus end-to-end recipes (AI script generation, opening a project, pulling responses, AI analysis, webhook signature verification) with copy-paste curl. Start here.
- [API Documentation](https://api.subo.ai/docs): Interactive Scalar UI with full endpoint reference
- [OpenAPI Spec](https://api.subo.ai/v1/openapi.json): Raw OpenAPI 3.1.0 JSON spec — machine-readable
- [Get an API Key](https://app.subo.gg/app/account): Generate keys in the Community account tab, under API Access
- [Subo Homepage](https://subo.gg/): Product overview and feature list
- [Discord Forms](https://subo.gg/forms/): How Subo replaces a Google Form or Typeform link in a Discord server: applications, sign-ups, bug reports and feedback asked one question at a time, with skip logic, three privacy modes, role targeting, and a web link for people without a Discord account, beside the Discord post or on its own.
- [Pricing](https://subo.gg/pricing): Plans (FREE, PREMIUM, VIP, CUSTOM) and rate limits per tier
- [Blog](https://subo.gg/blog): News and updates

## Templates

Subo ships ready-made, cloneable survey, poll, and quiz templates. Each has a public landing page and can be cloned into a community from the web app, or built programmatically via the API.

- [Template gallery](https://subo.gg/templates): Browse all templates by goal (Engage, Understand, Get things done).
- [Template catalog (JSON)](https://subo.gg/templates.json): Machine-readable list of every template with slugs, showcased features, and clone links. This is the canonical, always-current list.

Example templates:
- [Event Prediction Contest](https://subo.gg/templates/event-prediction-contest): Turn any match, tournament, or awards night into a prediction game with scoring, grading, and score-based XP rewards.
- [Lore Trivia Quiz](https://subo.gg/templates/lore-trivia-quiz): Quiz a community on any body of knowledge with automatic grading, per-answer feedback, and an achievement for everyone who passes.

## What the API Does

Authentication: `X-API-Key` request header (scoped to a community). Rate limits: 60–1,000 req/min depending on tier.
Idempotency: Send `Idempotency-Key: <UUIDv4>` header on all write operations

Key resources:
- **Projects** — Create, manage, open, close, clone surveys and polls
- **Script & Blocks** — Build survey scripts (single choice, multiple choice, open text, numeric, content, action and calculated blocks)
- **Responses** — Retrieve paginated respondent answers
- **Analysis** — Aggregated stats and AI summarization of open-ended answers
- **Communities** — Manage community settings such as accomplishments, XP and default survey settings
- **Members** — View all community members and manage their XP, access levels and accomplishments
- **Webhooks** — Real-time event subscriptions (project lifecycle, response submitted, analysis completed)
- **AI Generation** — Auto-generate a full survey script from a plain-text intent description, in any language, using every block type plus skip logic and scoring; optional plan step (`POST /communities/{communityId}/projects/generate/plan`)
- **API Keys** — Create and revoke scoped keys (REST only; not exposed through MCP)

## Most Useful Endpoints for AI Agents

All paths below are relative to `https://api.subo.ai/v1`. Almost every endpoint is
nested under a community: resolve `{communityId}` first with `GET /communities`.

1. **Create Project (with AI script generation)**
   - `POST /communities/{communityId}/projects`
   - Use `intent` field for natural language → full script (e.g. "Measure member satisfaction after the last event")
   - `type` is `convo` (multi-question survey) or `poll`
   - `question_count` is optional (the model picks what the goal needs, capped at 20 and the plan's limit); `max_blocks` is a deprecated alias
   - `quality` is `quick` or `deep`; omitted, it defaults to `deep` on a paid plan, which costs far more credits (typically ~24,000-48,000 vs ~700). Set it explicitly in automation
   - `language` accepts any language name or code (default: a language the intent names, then the community's); `facts` passes dates, results or odds the draft should use as written (no web search)
   - The response's `draft` object carries `author_notes`, `dropped` and `flagged` blocks, `model`, `credits_used` and `notices`
   - Alternative: Provide full `script.blocks` manually (mutually exclusive with `intent`)
   - Returns project + generated script; the project starts `inactive`

2. **Replace / Update Script**
   - `PUT /communities/{communityId}/projects/{projectId}/script`
   - Replace entire script when project is inactive
   - Per-block edits: `POST|PUT|DELETE .../script/blocks[/{blockId}]`

3. **Open Project**
   - `POST /communities/{communityId}/projects/{projectId}/open`
   - Makes the survey live. `delivery.entry_points` lists the ways into the
     project, each with its own rule; the Discord post and the web link are on
     independently. It is a list matched on `type`: send only the entry points you
     change, and an omitted field keeps its value. It is read back on create,
     update, open and every project read.
     - `discord_post`: members of the community's Discord server press the post.
       `enabled` is on when the project has `delivery.invitation.post_channel_id`.
       `answers_on` `discord`: they answer in Discord (thread or DM, see
       `answer_surfaces`); `web`: the post hands each of them a personal link and
       they answer on the web as themselves, even with the web link off.
       `required_role_ids` (any-of) gates every Discord check: where a member
       presses the post, and where someone verifies with Discord on a `verified`
       web link (checked live). Not checked on an `anyone` or `signed_in` link,
       nor for Twitch, YouTube or Steam sources.
     - `web_link`: anyone who has the link (`url`, same as `delivery.share_url`).
       `enabled`; `url` is read-only, null while the link is off.
       - `who` `anyone`: no sign-in. Identifies only respondents already signed
         in to Subo with Discord; set `privacy_mode: "anonymous"` to identify
         nobody.
       - `who` `signed_in`: a sign-in with one of `sign_in_with` (`discord`,
         `twitch`, `google`, `steam`; a platform Subo cannot offer yet is a 400
         listing the available ones). The person is named and nothing is checked;
         nothing to connect first. `google` is a Google account, not a YouTube
         channel. A new `signed_in` link without `sign_in_with` offers `discord`.
         One answer per account. Rewards (XP, roles, achievements) reach only
         Discord sign-ins.
       - `who` `verified`: a sign-in with one of `verified_source_ids`
         (`verified_sources` on read), membership checked, any one is enough. A
         Discord source checks server membership, Twitch checks follows, YouTube
         checks subscriptions, Steam checks that the person owns the game.
       - Turning the link on without `who` means `verified` with the community's
         Discord server.
     - `invitation`: read-only, on GET project: a journey step or a campaign that
       invites to the project (`source`, `campaign_id`, `name`, `step_name`,
       `status`). The invitation admits its member, whatever the post and the
       link say.
     - Example, Discord post in Discord plus an open link:
       `[{"type": "discord_post", "answers_on": "discord"}, {"type": "web_link", "enabled": true, "who": "anyone"}]`
     - A signed-in link with Twitch and Google:
       `{"type": "web_link", "enabled": true, "who": "signed_in", "sign_in_with": ["discord", "twitch", "google"]}`
     - A link for Discord members and Twitch followers:
       `{"type": "web_link", "enabled": true, "who": "verified", "verified_source_ids": [12, 34]}`
     - Polls have the Discord post only, answered in Discord.
   - `delivery.share_url` is the web link while `web_link` is on, and `null`
     while it is off, whatever the Discord post does.
   - Audience Sources (what a `verified` link checks against):
     `GET /communities/{communityId}/sources` lists them (`id`, `provider`
     discord/twitch/youtube/steam, `external_id`, `display_name`, `status`,
     `connected_at`); the `id` is what `verified_source_ids` takes. The
     community's Discord server is always there.
     `POST /communities/{communityId}/sources` connects a Steam game
     (`{"provider": "steam", "app_id": 1145360}`, Admin key). Twitch and YouTube
     need an Admin's browser sign-in in the dashboard (Settings > Networks) and
     cannot be connected through the API.
     `DELETE /communities/{communityId}/sources/{sourceId}` disconnects one.
   - Open refuses a project nobody can reach: with no post channel it opens
     without posting when its web link is on or a journey or campaign invites to
     it; with no post, no link and no invitation it returns `422 channel_required`.
   - Deprecated, still working: `delivery.audience` (`participation` /
     `response_channel`). Sending back the pair you read changes nothing; it
     cannot describe a post answered in Discord beside a web link. Never send it
     together with `entry_points` (that is a 400).
   - `delivery.answer_surfaces` orders WHERE a Discord post answered in Discord is answered, as a
     fallback chain tried first to last: `["dm","thread","web"]`. `dm` is a direct
     message from the bot, `thread` is a private thread in the server, `web` is
     a browser link. Each surface may appear once. `web` ends the chain: it
     cannot fail, so any surface listed after it is never reached (the API
     accepts such a chain rather than rejecting it — put `web` last).
     Only meaningful for a `discord_post` with `answers_on: discord`; stored but
     never consulted on the web. `answers_on: discord` with a chain that starts
     with `web` is refused (400). Avoid `thread` on an anonymous project — a thread is
     readable by anyone with Manage Threads.
   - `answer_surfaces` defaults to `null`, which is NOT an empty chain: it means
     no override, and Subo resolves the chain per press from the privacy mode.
     The DM is always tried first: an anonymous project resolves to
     `["dm","web"]`, any other project to `["dm","thread","web"]`. Send `null` to
     clear an override; `[]` returns a 400, as does a repeated surface.
   - Close early with `POST .../projects/{projectId}/close`
   - Colors are 6-digit hex WITHOUT `#` (`e1287e`): `delivery.invitation.border_color`
     and `border_color_closed`, and the community's `closing_embed_color` and
     `xp_closing_embed_color`. A leading `#` is accepted and removed; anything else is
     a 400 naming the field.
   - Achievement and role notices: `rewards.xp_achievement_announcement` on
     `PUT /communities/{communityId}` is a string. `""` turns notices off, `"-1"` is a
     DM (falling back to the member's private thread with Subo when their DMs are
     closed), `"-2"` is that private thread, and a Discord channel id posts in that
     public channel with a mention of the member. Any other value is a 400.

4. **List or Get Responses**
   - `GET /communities/{communityId}/projects/{projectId}/responses` (paginated; `per_page` max 100)
   - `GET /communities/{communityId}/projects/{projectId}/responses/{responseId}`
   - Join on `user_id` (globally unique); `platform_id` is only unique within its `provider` namespace
   - `provider` is WHO admitted the respondent: `discord`, `youtube`, `twitch`,
     `steam`, `patreon`, `google` or `web`. Verified respondents carry their
     platform, and so do respondents who signed in on a `signed_in` link (e.g.
     `google`); sessions from the Discord post are `discord`, unidentified
     `anyone`-link sessions are `web`.
   - `answered_in` is WHERE the session was answered: `thread`, `dm`, `web`, or
     `null`. A different axis from `provider`, which is WHO admitted the
     respondent, so a `youtube` respondent can answer on any of the three.
     `null` means NOT RECORDED, not `thread`: every session collected before this
     field existed reads `null`, so treating it as a default surface miscounts
     history. Returned on anonymous projects too, since where an interview
     happened is not respondent-identifying.
   - `privacy_mode: anonymous` redacts this endpoint: `user_id`, `platform_id` and
     `session_number` come back `null`, and the `response.submitted` webhook nulls the
     same three (matching the app's Responses tab and XLSX export). Respondent filters
     (`user_id`, `platform_id`, `session_number`) are refused with a 400 on an anonymous
     project rather than ignored. `id` still identifies one submission and stays valid for
     the single-response GET, and `provider` is still returned — the admitting source is
     not treated as identifying.

5. **Trigger AI Analysis**
   - `POST /communities/{communityId}/projects/{projectId}/analysis` (async; `{"force": true}` re-runs)
   - `GET` the same path for summaries plus aggregated stats and distributions
   - `total_sessions` = respondents (same as `pagination.total` on list responses); use it
     for "how many people answered". `total_responses` = individual answers across all
     blocks (one person answering 6 blocks counts 6); it is what the plan's response limit counts
   - Summaries are on/off per community, per project (`settings.text_analysis`) and per `open_text` block (`text_analysis`); a block that asks for personal data is off unless turned on explicitly
   - Respondents are sent to the model as codes (e.g. `R-7K3QXA`), never by name, and emails, phone numbers and similar data are removed first
   - `summary_status` can be `failed` (request again) or `skipped` (not enough credits; `text_analysis.credits_short_by` says how many)

6. **Webhooks** (Highly recommended for agents)
   - `POST /communities/{communityId}/webhooks` with `{url, name, events[]}`
   - `url` must be `https://` and resolve only to public addresses: loopback, private and
     link-local are refused on save and re-checked before every delivery; redirects are
     not followed
   - Events: `project.created`, `project.updated`, `project.opened`, `project.closed`,
     `project.status_changed`, `project.deleted`, `response.submitted`, `analysis.completed`
   - `signing_secret` is returned once. Deliveries carry `X-Subo-Event`, `X-Subo-Delivery`
     and `X-Subo-Signature: sha256=<hmac hex>` (HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body)
   - Retries at 30s, 5m, 30m, 2h, 8h; deliveries are at-least-once, so dedupe on `X-Subo-Delivery`

7. **Clone a Template**
   - `GET /templates`, then `POST /communities/{communityId}/templates/{templateId}/clone`
   - Deep clone (script, scoring, grading, action blocks); source-server bindings stripped

## Recipes (survey designs, on-domain)

End-to-end walkthroughs of real survey designs: the script, the action blocks, the
scoring, and the logic that ties them together. Served as plain markdown, so an agent can
fetch one and follow it directly. These are survey-*design* recipes; for API *mechanics*
(auth, pagination, webhook signatures) use https://subo.gg/api.

Canonical home: https://subo.gg/recipes (HTML, with FAQ and template cross-links).
The same ten are also fetchable as raw markdown from the API host, which is convenient
for agents but NOT canonical:
- `GET https://api.subo.ai/v1/recipes` — JSON index (slug, title, summary, url)
- `GET https://api.subo.ai/v1/recipes/{slug}` — full markdown for one recipe

- [Welcome quiz](https://subo.gg/recipes/welcome-quiz): Onboard new members by recording region, language and notification preferences; choices fire achievements linked to Discord roles.
- [Volunteer / moderator funnel](https://subo.gg/recipes/volunteer-moderator-funnel): Screening funnel where one decisive question gates mutually-exclusive Mod Trial vs Waitlist role grants.
- [Event RSVP with attendance streaks](https://subo.gg/recipes/event-rsvp-streak): RSVP funnel using session-scoped firing plus XP-threshold achievements to produce streak rewards without per-event tagging.
- [Playtester selection](https://subo.gg/recipes/playtester-selection): Recruit qualified playtesters via availability gating; qualifiers get a durable Beta Tester achievement and role.
- [Hogwarts house sorting quiz](https://subo.gg/recipes/hogwarts-house-sorting-quiz): Personality-style sorting via argmax over hidden buckets, assigning one outcome role.
- [Member segmentation](https://subo.gg/recipes/member-segmentation): Segment a community into personas using the same hidden-bucket argmax pattern.
- [Study quiz](https://subo.gg/recipes/study-quiz): Graded quiz using correct_answer_index with when_correct / when_incorrect feedback branches.
- [World capitals quiz](https://subo.gg/recipes/world-capitals-quiz): Knowledge quiz with per-answer grading and scored leaderboard results.
- [Prediction poll](https://subo.gg/recipes/prediction-poll): Prediction contest where option weights price risk, so unlikely correct calls score higher.
- [Pre/post assessment](https://subo.gg/recipes/pre-post-assessment): Measure change over time with twin projects capped at one completion per user each.

## Key Features Agents Love
- **AI Script Generation**: Turn a plain-text goal into a complete multi-block survey script in one call.
- **Real-time Webhooks**: Get notified instantly when new responses arrive or analysis is ready.
- **Rich Script System**: Supports single/multiple choice, open text, numeric, rating, opinion scale, NPS, ranking, conditional logic (structured `show_when` / `hide_when`, compiled to a precondition), and content, action and calculated blocks. The block-type list at the bottom of this file is the complete set the API accepts; a Discord-only question type such as yes/no is sent as `single_punch`.
- **Ordered question types that store numbers**: `rating`, `opinion_scale` and `nps` store the picked integer, so analysis returns a real average and distribution rather than option counts. `ranking` stores one row per ranked item, `value` = the rank position.
- **Analysis**: Built-in AI summarization of qualitative answers.

## Best Practices for Agents
- Always include `Idempotency-Key` on POST/PUT/DELETE operations.
- Use webhooks instead of polling for new responses and analysis results.
- Start with the `intent` field when creating projects — it’s the fastest way to generate high-quality surveys.
- Handle `402` errors gracefully (insufficient bot credits for AI features).

Base URL: https://api.subo.ai
Version: /v1/ (non-breaking changes in-place; breaking changes under /v2/)
Idempotency: Pass `Idempotency-Key` (UUID v4) header on write operations.
Block types: `single_punch`, `multi_punch`, `open_text`, `open_numeric`, `rating`, `opinion_scale`, `nps`, `ranking`, `content_block`, `action_block`, `calculated_block`.
Scale family: point range is the block's `min` / `max`; whole-scale presentation is the `scale` object (`icon`, `label_left`, `label_center`, `label_right`). On a scale, `options[].value` is the point number as a string and carries that point's `emoji` or `label` — a plain star or number scale sends no options at all. `answer_style` is `buttons` | `select_menu` on the three scales, `full_text` | `emoji_only` on `ranking`; `rank_top_n` (ranking only) asks for a partial ranking.
Privacy modes: `transparent`, `semi-private`, `anonymous` (omitting `privacy_mode` inherits the community's configured default, `anonymous` for a community that never changed it — set it explicitly when anonymity matters).
Errors: `400 invalid_request`, `402 payment_required` (out of bot credits / tier-gated), `403 forbidden`, `404 not_found`, `429 rate_limit_exceeded` (honor `Retry-After`).

Worked examples with copy-paste curl for all of the above: https://subo.gg/api
Survey-design recipes (ten worked walkthroughs): https://subo.gg/recipes
